A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ARPG, with matching authors, core architecture, and overlapping experiments. Their complete main texts and appendices support comparison; equations, tables, figures, and qualitative samples are readable.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet generation results, controllable generation results, architectural ablations, decoding experiments, and zero-shot image examples (Tables 2–7 and supplementary figures).

after.justification: v2 reports original image-generation experiments and ablations, plus text-to-image results, attention analyses, and training-loss curves (Tables 2–5 and 8; Figures 3 and 9–12).

M1.justification: The two-pass decoder, randomized training, and shared KV design already appear in v1. v2 adds text conditioning through pretrained FLAN-T5-XL embeddings (Section 4.2), extending the input procedure. Its fuller description of block-wise Pass-1 inference does not establish whether that behavior was already present in v1's underspecified inference implementation.

E1.justification: v2 retains ImageNet generation at both resolutions, edge/depth conditioning, and zero-shot manipulation. It adds caption-conditioned generation using a 4M-image BLIP-3o subset, GenEval evaluation, and diverse text-to-image examples (Sections 4.1–4.2; Figures 7 and 12), substantially extending the represented data and task requirements.

E2.justification: v2 Table 2 adds NAR-L/XL/XXL and removes the 256-resolution LDM-4, VQGAN-re, RQ-Transformer-re, and AiM comparisons; ADM disappears from the 512-resolution comparison. New Table 3 compares text-to-image ARPG with LlamaGen-XL, Chameleon, and SD-v1.5. ControlVAR-d24 is also removed from Table 4.

E3.justification: v2 introduces text-to-image training for 50 epochs and GenEval evaluation, causal-versus-block-wise inference controls, and sampling at 16 and 24 steps. For retained experiments, reported AdamW beta1 changes from 0.99 to 0.9, and v1 Algorithm 2's cosine sampling schedule becomes arccos in v2 Appendix A. These documented revisions do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Existing decoder-allocation, KV-sharing, sampling-step, and generation-order analyses are retained or relocated. v2 adds positional-encoding ablation, controlled attention-pattern comparisons (Figure 9 and Table 8), training-loss scaling analysis (Figure 10), and RandAR/ARPG attention maps (Figures 3 and 11), substantially expanding investigation of the method's mechanisms.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, statistical error bars, or significance tests. The additional curves and attention maps in v2 introduce no statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 2's reported ImageNet FIDs at 64 steps change from 2.44/2.10/1.94 to 2.37/1.99/1.86 for L/XL/XXL. The 512-resolution XL FID changes from 3.38 to 2.82. v2 also adds text-to-image results, including overall GenEval 0.31, and extensive attention-control results. Because reported settings change, these replacements cannot uniformly be interpreted as gains under identical protocols.

T1.justification: v1 Insight 2 makes an unqualified claim that unmasked-token queries receive no gradients. v2 Section 3.1 and Appendix C restrict the zero-gradient derivation to the final layer and explicitly acknowledge indirect gradients in shallower layers. The derivative calculation is largely retained, but its scope is substantively corrected.

C1.justification: v2 extends the main contributions to text-to-image generation, which v1's conclusion explicitly leaves for future work. Its abstract also strengthens the quantitative headline from FID 1.94 at 64 steps and over 20-fold throughput to FID 1.83 at 32 steps and over 30-fold speedup. The central random-order parallel-generation claim remains.

C2.justification: v2 develops new interpretations connecting negligible attention to masked tokens with computational redundancy, and block-wise inference context with improved fidelity (Section 3 and Appendix B). It distinguishes optimal FID at 32 steps from visual quality at 64 steps and interprets the scaling curves. The previous absence of text-to-image validation is replaced by experiments and discussion of further scaling.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix A substantially expands configuration disclosure with model-specific iterations, batch sizes, weight decay, augmentation, and sampling settings. It identifies the controllable-generation ViT adapter and its exclusion from parameter counts. Appendices D–E add text-to-image sampling details and explicit decoder-pass pseudocode. Some earlier specifics, including the 0.1 class-conditioning dropout, are no longer stated.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around acceleration, comparing fixed-block methods, flexible schedules, and attention patterns in Section 2.2 and Table 1. New references include SAR, NAR, speculative Jacobi decoding, and the text-to-image dataset, encoder, and evaluation framework. Several broader masked-modeling and linear-attention references are removed; the changes exceed bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The introduction and method are extensively rewritten around content representation and position-guided prediction, with revised terminology and experimental organization. Controllable-generation and zero-shot implementation explanations move into the main method; the gradient proof and generation-order study move into appendices. The conclusion is substantially shortened, and the pseudocode is reorganized.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to a single-column layout, with redrawn comparison and architecture diagrams. v1 Tables 2–3 merge into v2 Table 2, and the architecture table becomes an expanded appendix configuration table. Sample grids are consolidated, while attention maps, decoding/scaling plots, and text-to-image panels substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important weaknesses in v1 through substantially fuller configuration disclosure, a properly qualified gradient argument, and controlled attention-pattern experiments that better test the proposed mechanism. Text-to-image experiments also validate an application previously left untested. Together these substantially strengthen reproducibility, mathematical precision, and empirical support. Reporting weaknesses remain, including unexplained IS discrepancies between Tables 2 and 8—for example, 297.7 versus 287.90 for ARPG-L at 32 steps—and incomplete text-to-image configuration details.
